::: {#exm-logarithm}
#### Some logarithms

By @def-logarithm,

- $\log_2 16 = 4$, since $2^4 = 16$;
- $\log_2 1 = 0$, since $2^0 = 1$;
- $\log_{10} 1000 = 3$, since $10^3 = 1000$;
- $\log_2 2^n = n$ for every integer $n$.

The logarithm $\log_2 n$ grows by 1 each time $n$ doubles:
$\log_2 (2 n) = \log_2 n + 1$, since $2^{\log_2 n + 1} = 2 \cdot 2^{\log_2 n} = 2 n$.

:::
